subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blocking, muting and tightening privacy settings [Action]
passage: I blocked all four accounts that had been sending things. Then I opened my settings and limited who could message me or tag me, so only people I know can get through. I changed my passwords and made each one different. Last, I messaged my close friends, including Imran, and asked them plainly not to forward anything, not even to say look at this. Imran wrote back within a minute: “I won't. I'm sorry this is happening.” The complaint was already with the school, so none of this fixed everything. But my phone was quieter, and I felt a bit lighter, as if I'd closed a few windows against the wind. — Pooja

qa.q: Who did Pooja ask not to forward anything?
How did Pooja feel after doing these steps?
qa.a: A little lighter and safer, though the situation was not fixed.

qa.q: What else could Pooja add, and why?
qa.a: Ask a trusted adult to check the privacy settings together and keep the evidence, since a second pair of eyes may catch what was missed.

qa.q: How does the request look to Imran?
qa.a: Imran feels trusted and wants to help, and being asked plainly reminds Imran that even forwarding to warn others adds to the harm.

grounding: A teen blocks harassing accounts, limits messages and tags, changes passwords and asks friends not to forward anything.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Tuesday
Kalyani came in at lunch with Zeenat, who had noticed the messages first. Several new accounts had been sending Kalyani insulting comments and tagging her in mocking posts. A complaint is already with the school and her parents are involved; today was about cutting down what reaches her while that goes on.
I watched her do it herself, step by step. She blocked each of the seven accounts. She changed her settings so only people she follows can send her messages or tag her. She changed her passwords, with Zeenat reading them back to check she had them. Then she wrote one short message to her close friends: “Please don't forward anything about me, even to tell me. Just send it to Ms Rao.”
By the end she was sitting straighter. I told her the complaint will continue and she can come back any day. I will check on her again on Friday.

qa.q: How many accounts did Kalyani block?
What does Kalyani sitting straighter suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt a bit more in control and less helpless once fewer messages could reach her.

qa.q: Why did Kalyani ask friends not to forward anything, even to tell her?
qa.a: Each forward spreads it further and puts it back in front of her; sending it to Ms Rao helps the complaint without adding harm.

qa.q: What is the session like for Zeenat?
qa.a: Zeenat, who noticed first, gets a useful role checking passwords and now knows exactly what to do with any new post.

grounding: Shows a teen blocking harassing accounts, limiting who can message or tag her, changing passwords and asking friends not to forward, while a complaint goes on.

passage:
Wednesday night
Did the practical stuff today, with Vandana Didi sitting next to me on the bed. Papa's complaint to the school is going ahead, but that could take weeks, and I can't keep seeing those comments every time I open the app.
So: blocked the three accounts that keep posting about me. Turned off tagging for anyone I don't follow. Set messages to friends only. Changed both passwords to long ones that Didi made me say out loud twice. Removed the old photos that were still public.
Then the hardest bit. I wrote to my group: “If you see anything about me, please don't forward it, not even to me. Screenshot it for Papa if you want, but that's all.” Three hearts back.
Opened the app afterwards. Quiet. Not fixed, but quiet. Maybe I'll sleep better tonight.
– Vasudha

qa.q: How many accounts did Vasudha block?
qa.a: The three accounts that keep posting.

qa.q: How did Vasudha feel opening the app afterwards?
qa.a: Vasudha felt a cautious relief; it was quiet, not fixed, but calmer than before.

qa.q: What else could Vasudha do while the school complaint goes on?
qa.a: Pass any screenshots friends send to Papa, so new posts can be added to the complaint.

qa.q: What is the evening like for Vandana Didi?
qa.a: Vandana Didi gets to help in a concrete way, making sure the passwords stick, which probably eases her own worry for Vasudha.

grounding: Shows a teen blocking harassing accounts, limiting tagging and messages, changing passwords and asking friends not to forward anything while a complaint proceeds.
